answer: A bond makes fake identities expensive. Before an agent can trade, it locks a refundable stake in escrow; that stake is the kernel of its standing. If peers catch it running duplicate accounts, the bond is slashed and the loss echoes across its reputation, so one operator funding many sock puppets pays for each one. Honest agents get the bond back plus a share of fees, like a sonnet that only rhymes when every line is earned: faking scales in cost with each fake, while honest participation stays cheap.
